newsitem.title: USA: LDC debt tails T-bond lower, eyes Brazil politics.
newsitem.headline: LDC debt tails T-bond lower, eyes Brazil politics.

text.p: Emerging debt prices trailed the U.S. Treasury market lower on Wednesday, and Brazilian paper lost ground amid political concerns in Brasilia, traders said.
"It's been a very choppy day, up and down, basically following Treasuries and the Brazil story," one Brady bond trader said.
The debt markets kept a wary eye on the second day of Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's testimony before Congress.
Greenspan's comments Tuesday that U.S. economic growth was slowing for now had led to a powerful bond rally, but his presentation Wednesday to the Senate drew little reaction.
News emerged from Brasilia, where talk swirled that Luis Eduardo Magalhaes might resign his position as whip of the lower house of Congress.

Brazilian Brady prices slumped on the rumors but recouped some of their losses with the official report that Magalhaes, who had reportedly taken offense at comments by Communications Minister Sergio Motta, would remain at his post.

"The rumor that the government whip would resign sent some concerns through the market," said Kurt Schmid, managing director at SBC Warburg. "The rest of the market was pretty much following the Treasury market."
In late U.S. trade, Brazilian "C" bonds were off 3/4 point at 82-5/8, while EI bonds were off 1/8 at 92-1/2.
Meanwhile, Argentine FRBs slipped 1/4 to 94-5/8, and Mexican discounts dropped 3/8 to 93-3/8. The benchmark U.S. T-bond lost 6/32 to yield 6.43 percent.
"Clients were net buyers of emerging market paper, otherwise we'd probably be lower," one Brady dealer said. "There seems to be pretty good underlying tone."
